lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The portfolio link appears to use a placeholder domain.
items.because: A dead or generic link undermines the resume.

items.says: Put the experience entries in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Voltline is the more recent role, and listing Clearwater first makes the timeline harder to scan.

items.says: Make date and location formatting consistent and distinguish project dates from employment dates.
Clarify the gap between graduation and the first listed role if relevant.
items.because: The dates show a gap from May 2021 to April 2022.

items.says: Consider adding relevant coursework or academic projects.
items.because: They may help an early-career application if they add evidence not shown elsewhere.

items.says: Clarify what “test time per unit” measures and whether the comparison covers the same test scope.
Make clear that 20,000 units a month is volume processed, not a performance result.
Clarify the basis for attributing the failures to the solder-paste change.
items.because: Otherwise, the reduction may sound more conclusive than the evidence supports.

items.says: Define the return-rate measurement period or denominator.
items.because: Otherwise, the reduction may sound more conclusive than the evidence supports.

items.says: Define a “drift complaint” and the period used to compare the counts.
items.because: Complaint counts can be affected by production volume or reporting practices.

items.says: Clarify whether the throughput figures are measured production results or station capacity.
Clarify whether the throughput figures refer to boards or finished units.
Say whether quality or retest rates changed.
Specify what “update speed” measures and the conditions of the comparison.
items.because: “Speed” could mean elapsed time, transfer rate, or completion rate.

items.says: Explain what the 400 tests cover and what running on every build means in practice.
items.because: Test count alone does not indicate coverage or reliability.

items.says: Clarify how much of the test process you owned.
items.because: Test count alone does not show ownership.

items.says: Clarify what sensor data the logger captured and how it isolated the five failures.
Be ready to explain how data was buffered and written to flash without affecting the system.
The 5 kHz-at-8 kHz sampling claim needs correction or substantiation.
items.because: Sampling a 5 kHz component at 8 kHz does not satisfy the Nyquist criterion.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter `volatile` does not by itself fix a race condition.
items.because: It does not make access atomic.

items.says: Substantiate your role, the rewrite’s scope, and the jitter and fault measurements.
The firmware-rewrite result appears again in the Formula Student section.
items.because: The duplication creates a serious credibility problem.

items.says: Add defensible hardware, firmware, and power-measurement specifics to the weather-station project.
items.because: Readers otherwise have little beyond the headline result to assess the work.

items.says: Remove the “next-generation” and “redefines” promotional claim.
items.because: It sounds like marketing and does not establish what you built.

items.says: Document the current-measurement conditions and what changed between readings.
items.because: Battery, radio activity, sampling frequency, and measurement method can affect average current.

items.says: Make the published repository or documentation accessible from the header link.
Verify the extent of the school’s use without implying broader adoption.
items.because: The stated evidence supports two builds.

items.says: Ensure the project bullets support the “Electronics Lead” role and fit the Formula Student scope.
The robot-fleet description appears inconsistent with the Formula Student car project.
items.because: It may have been carried over from the Voltline role.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the dashboard CAN work.
items.because: The passive phrasing does not show what you implemented, tested, or owned.

items.says: The 300-robot firmware claim duplicates the Voltline accomplishment and conflicts with this project’s context.
items.because: The Formula Student car project has earlier dates and is not described as a robot fleet.

items.says: Expand the sparse skills section selectively with relevant, demonstrable technical skills.
items.because: It is sparse compared with the experience claimed.

items.says: Replace broad areas such as “firmware” and “low-power design” with more concrete skills.
items.because: They repeat areas of experience rather than making the technical toolkit easy to scan.
